author: Brian Parsons
title: Lake Taylor's Bobby Pannenbacker retiring after 53-year career in HS athletics - NewsBreak
text:
By Brian Parsons ,
5 hours ago
NORFOLK, Va. (WAVY) — Running a high school athletic department involves serious dedication, and no one has more dedicated than Lake Taylor athletic director Bobby Pannenbacker, who is retiring later this month after 25 years.
“It’s time,” Pannenbacker said. “I’m 75 years old and I’ve been doing this for 53 years.”
Prior to his time at Lake Taylor, Pannenbacker worked at Norfolk Academy, Northside Middle School and was a PE teacher and head football coach at Maury High School from 1987 to 1996.
After his stint at Maury, he worked with the late Bert Harrell and helped fill a void in Norfolk by starting up a full-fledged middle school sports program.
“We needed to play catch-up. We were out front compared to some of the other school systems except for Virginia Beach,” Pannenbacker said. “That was the key thing, building the middle school sports programs so that you have more successful high school programs, getting them indoctrinated early.”
At Lake Taylor, some of the things he’s overseen include a new turf football field, a new track and a refurbished basketball gymnasium. He’s also seen serious success, including nine state championships across boys and girls basketball and football.
“The joy of the kids performing on that stage has been the greatest joy,” he said, “watching them celebrate their success. This job has always been for the kids, and I’m sure Kenny will make sure it’s for the kids.”
Kenny would be Pannenbacker’s successor, Kenny Brown. He’s a former state champion basketball coach at Lake Taylor and, after working under Pannenbacker for two decades, it’s his turn to run the show.
“Those are very big shoes to fill,” Brown said. “But I think with me being his assistant for 20 years I might be able to fill those shoes earlier.”
Pannenbacker’s last day is June 30 as he begins life’s latest chapter.
“I have a lot of things I want to do, a lot of places I want to see and a lot of things I’m interested in that I have not had enough time to do,” Pannenbacker said, “and I’m looking forward to that. I really am.”
